Abidan
uh-BYE-dan
proper noun
Hebrew Abidan (H27), my father is judge — from ab (H1), father, and din (H1777), to judge, to plead a cause, to contend for the right.

Biblical Definition

Abidan the son of Gideoni was prince and captain of the tribe of Benjamin during the wilderness years. The LORD named him to stand with Moses at the numbering (Num 1:11); he commanded Benjamin's camp on the west with Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Rachel keeping together (Num 2:22); he brought his tribe's offering on the ninth day of the altar's dedication (Num 7:60, 65); and he led Benjamin's host when the standards moved (Num 10:24). No word of his is recorded and no deed outside the office. The name is the substance: my father is judge. Set against Gideoni his father, whose name means hewer, the household confession runs from demolition to justice — the idols cut down, and the LORD Himself seated as the One who tries the cause. Din is not merely to pass verdict; it is to take up a case and see right done for the one who cannot get it for himself. So Abraham could ask, Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? (Gen 18:25), and Israel could sing, he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness (Psa 96:13). For a Benjamite of the wilderness generation to be called my father is judge was to say that the final word on his life would be spoken not by Egypt, nor by Canaan, nor by the congregation, but by God.

Origin & Era

Prince and captain of the tribe of Benjamin in the wilderness, son of Gideoni; his name means my father is judge.

expand to see more

ABIDAN, Hebrew Abidan, my father is judge.

Son of Gideoni, of the tribe of Benjamin.

Named by the LORD to assist Moses and Aaron in numbering the congregation.

Captain of Benjamin, which encamped on the west of the tabernacle with Ephraim and Manasseh.

He offered for his tribe on the ninth day of the dedication of the altar.

Key Scripture

Num 1:11 — "Of Benjamin; Abidan the son of Gideoni."

Num 2:22 — "Then the tribe of Benjamin: and the captain of the sons of Benjamin shall be Abidan the son of Gideoni."

Num 7:65 — "And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this was the offering of Abidan the son of Gideoni."

Num 10:24 — "And over the host of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan the son of Gideoni."

Modern Corruption

Divine judgment is treated as incompatible with divine love; Scripture makes God's judging the very reason the oppressed may hope.

expand to see more

The judgment of God is the doctrine the modern mind most wishes to retire. It is presented as a relic of a harsher religion, unworthy of a God of love, and the preaching that names it is called severe. The objection misunderstands the word. Din and its Greek counterparts do not primarily mean condemnation; they mean the taking up of a case so that right is done. That is why the Psalms greet the coming Judge with singing rather than dread: let the floods clap their hands… before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth (Psa 98:8-9). A world in which God will not judge is a world in which every wrong done to the weak stands forever unanswered.

The doctrine is severe in exactly one direction, and Scripture does not soften it: it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment (Heb 9:27), and the judgment is according to truth. What the gospel offers is not the cancellation of the assize but a substitute at the bar — there is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus (Rom 8:1), because the condemnation fell on Him. To confess with Abidan that my father is judge is therefore terror or comfort depending entirely on whether one stands in Adam or in Christ, and it is the business of preaching to make that difference plain.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Abidan (H27), from ab (H1), father, and din (H1777), to judge, to plead a cause.

expand to see more

Hebrew ab (H1) — father; the element opening many Israelite names (Abidan, Abinadab, Abiezer).

Hebrew din (H1777) — to judge, to contend, to plead the cause of; not merely to sentence but to see right done.

Hebrew Abidan (H27) — my father is judge; the prince of Benjamin, Numbers 1:11, 2:22, 7:60, 7:65, 10:24.

Hebrew shaphat (H8199) — to judge, to govern; Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? (Gen 18:25).

Greek krino (G2919) — to judge, to decide; we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ (2Co 5:10).
